lines.japanese: 日曜、夜。グローヴ街は若者たちの喧騒で溢れていた。
lines.english: Sunday night. Grove Street overflowed with the clamor of young people.

lines.japanese: 「んまー！　ねね、これマジでんまくない？　ちょお高級ビーフステーキ並じゃない？　ねー良かったっしょ、こんな美味しいの、おごってもらって！」
lines.english: Mmm! Hey, isn't this, like, seriously good? As good as some crazy-expensive steak, right? See, aren't you glad I treated you?

lines.japanese: 「たしかに……これはこれで美味いんだけど……」
lines.english: “It is... good, in its own way...”

lines.japanese: ここはイタ飯屋やらダイニングバーやらが並んだオサレな一画だ。そろそろ時間もいい頃だから、若者たちは思い思いの飲食店へ吸いこまれてゆく。
lines.english: This was a trendy little strip lined with Italian joints and dining bars. It was about that time, so young people were filing into whichever place they felt like.

lines.japanese: だが俺たちが腰を下ろした場所は、丸椅子のカウンター席でも、店員に案内されて座るボックスシートのテーブルでもなく、適当に見つけた商業ビルの屋外階段だった。
lines.english: But we hadn't taken stools at a counter or been shown to a booth by a waiter. We were sitting on the outdoor stairs of some commercial building we'd found at random.

lines.japanese: 「で、何これ。何なのこの、パンに薄い肉とピクルス挟んだだけのジャンクな食物」
lines.english: “So what is this? What's this junk that's just a thin piece of meat and a pickle stuck between two bits of bread?”

lines.japanese: 「ハンバーガー。え、嫌いだった？」
lines.english: “A hamburger. What, you don't like them?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、嫌いじゃねーけど……」
lines.english: Nah, it's not like I hate it, but...

lines.japanese: おまえさっき超高級料理って言わなかった？
lines.english: Didn't you just call this super-fancy food?

lines.japanese: ま、いいけどな。もともと学生の経済力に過度な期待は抱いてなかったし。
lines.english: Eh, whatever. Wasn't like I'd expected much from a student's budget in the first place.

lines.japanese: 半額クーポン使用でバーガーセット２４０円。それでもこいつの財布事情からすれば、結構な額なのかもしれない。俺は表面が濡れてきたバーガーにかぶりついた。
lines.english: A burger combo for 240 yen with a half-price coupon. Even that might've been a lot for her wallet. I bit into the burger, the bun already getting soggy.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、ごめん！　そっか、もっとボリュームあるのが良かった？」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry! Did you want something more filling?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、いいって」
lines.english: “No, it’s fine.”

lines.japanese: 「えー？　ちゃんと食べんとー。なんか少食の男の子って、体力使ってなさげで頼りなーい」
lines.english: “Really? You gotta eat right. Guys who barely eat don't look like they use much energy. So unreliiiable.”

lines.japanese: おまえ……自分でバーガー選んどいて……。
lines.english: You... were the one who picked burgers...

lines.japanese: 「食ってるよ。ふだんは牛丼とかラーメンとかバリバリ食ってるっつの」
lines.english: “I eat. Normally I put away beef bowls and ramen like nobody's business.”

lines.japanese: 選考基準は安さと量。それ以外はわりとどうでもいい。
lines.english: Cheap and filling. That was all I cared about.

lines.japanese: 「えー、でもラーメン屋系ってなんか敷居高くない？」
lines.english: “But don't ramen shops feel kinda intimidating?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんで」
lines.english: “Huh? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「雰囲気、なんか男子校じゃん。あと床ぬるぬるするしー、トイレ男女兼用のトコ多いしー」
lines.english: “The whole atmosphere is like an all-boys school. And the floors are greasy, and loads of them have unisex bathrooms.”

lines.japanese: あー、まー、比率的にはそういう店多いかも？　べつにそんなん気になんねーけどなあ。
lines.english: Uh, yeah, I guess a lot of the places I went were like that? Never bothered me, though.

lines.japanese: 「でも美味しいとこあったら行ってみたいけどね」
lines.english: “Still, if there's somewhere really good, I'd like to try it.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、だったら花水木通りにいい屋台あるよ」
lines.english: “In that case, there's a good ramen cart on Flowering Dogwood Street.”

lines.japanese: 「ほんと？　わ、行きたい、隼人君こんど連れてってよ」
lines.english: “Really? Oh, I wanna go. Take me sometime, Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 「いいけど」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: いいけど。じゃねーっつの。くそっ、こいつ誘い方うめえな。鷲介みたいでしゃらくせえや。
lines.english: *Sure*, my ass. Damn it, she was good at slipping invitations past me. Sly as Shusuke. What a pain.

lines.japanese: 「あーそーだ、悪りい。俺あんま最近ラーメン好きじゃねえんだった」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Sorry. I haven't really been into ramen lately.”

lines.japanese: 「そーなん？　じゃ何がオキニだー？」
lines.english: “Really? So what's your fave these days?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんかアレ、あの、高くてオサレなやつ」
lines.english: “Uh, you know. That stuff. Expensive and stylish.”

lines.japanese: どうせ「ラーメンは好きじゃない」自体が嘘なので、俺は適当なことを言った。
lines.english: Since ‘I'm not into ramen’ was already a lie, I said the first thing that came to mind.

lines.japanese: 「なんでもいいんだけど、なんつうか、漠然と高くてオサレなやつ。あのー、ビフテキとか？」
lines.english: “Anything's fine. Just vaguely expensive and stylish. Like, uh... steak?”

lines.japanese: 「あとオマールエビ的なアレとか、あとメロン……あの皮がザラザラしてる方のメロンとか、あとオ、オ、オードブルとか」
lines.english: “Or that lobster thing. And melon... the kind with the rough skin. And h-h-hors d'oeuvres.”

lines.japanese: 「オードブルって食べ物の名前だっけ？」
lines.english: “Is hors d'oeuvres the name of a food?”

lines.japanese: 「え、違うの」
lines.english: “Wait, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「ワカラン、忘れたかも。私フランス料理なんか食べんもん」
lines.english: “Dunno. Maybe I forgot. I never eat French food.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ……だよな……」
lines.english: “Yeah... Of course...”

lines.japanese: 無性に白メシと味噌汁とタクアンが恋しくなった。お箸の国のひとだもの。
lines.english: I was suddenly overcome with longing for white rice, miso soup, and pickled daikon. I was a man from the land of chopsticks, after all.

lines.japanese: 「なに食ったところで腹に入れば同じだしな」
lines.english: “Doesn't matter what you eat once it's in your stomach.”

lines.japanese: 「言える言えるー。はい、あーん」
lines.english: “So true. Here, say ahh.”

lines.japanese: 「邪魔。そんで、買い物ってなに買うの」
lines.english: “You're in the way. So what are we buying?”

lines.japanese: 香田の差しだした一かけらは無視して、手元のバーガーにかぶりついた。やつは平然と答える。
lines.english: I ignored the morsel Koda held out and bit into the burger in my hand. She answered without concern.

lines.japanese: 「なんもー？　今月もう余裕ないし」
lines.english: “Nothing. I'm already broke this month.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なんも買わねーのに、なんで俺、買い物付きあわされてんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? If you're not buying anything, why am I getting dragged around on a shopping trip?”

lines.japanese: 「モノ買うだけが買い物じゃないじゃん。見るだけだって買い物じゃん」
lines.english: “Buying stuff isn't the only kind of shopping. Looking is shopping too.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、おまえ的な定義はどうでもいいんだけど、ウィンドウショッピングだったら、もっと気の合う女友達と行けよ。てっきり俺、荷物持ちとか値段交渉のために連れてこられたンだと──」
lines.english: “I don't care about your personal definition. If we're window-shopping, go with some girl you actually click with. I figured you'd brought me to carry bags or haggle over prices—”

lines.japanese: 「食べた」
lines.english: “You ate it.”
“—Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「そのバーガー、仕事代。食べたんだからお仕事しよーよ」
lines.english: “That burger was your fee. You ate it, so do your job.”

lines.japanese: 「ああまあ……そうな……」
lines.english: “Well... Yeah...”

lines.japanese: 俺は腰を浮かしかけていたが、観念して座りなおした。たしかにここで帰ったら契約違反だ。
lines.english: I had begun to rise, but I surrendered and sat back down. Leaving now really would be a breach of contract.
I sighed.

lines.japanese: もそもそ食いながら脱力する。
lines.english: I sagged as I chewed.

lines.japanese: 実はさっき香田に「その辺どっか座る？」と聞かれたとき、俺がこの場所を選んだのは偶然じゃなかった。
lines.english: The truth was, when Koda asked earlier if we should sit somewhere, I hadn't picked this place by accident.

lines.japanese: 小物屋とデザート屋を結ぶこのカーブ階段は、一年ぐらい前から俺定番の脱力スポットになっていたんだ。
lines.english: For about a year now, these curved stairs between a knickknack shop and a dessert place had been my regular place to unwind.

lines.japanese: 聴覚を全方位に開いて、適当に雑踏の向こうを眺める。意識をどこか一点へ絞らないのがコツだ。または「ボーッとすること」を意識するというか。
lines.english: I opened my ears in every direction and stared vaguely past the crowd. The trick was not focusing on any one thing. Or maybe consciously trying to zone out.

lines.japanese: 俺はここでそうしていると、だんだん自我が薄れて街に溶けこんでしまえる気がするんだ──
lines.english: When I sat here like this, little by little I could feel my sense of self thinning until I dissolved into the city—

lines.japanese: ──まあ、こんな話をしたのはおまえが初めてだけどな。どうせ分かるやつなんていないだろ。
lines.english: —though you're the first person I've ever told. Not that anybody would understand.

lines.japanese: 「隼人君？　どしたん？」
lines.english: “Hayato? What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「あー？　んー」
lines.english: “Huh? Mm.”

lines.japanese: 通行人Ａとなって遊んでいます。言えるかバカヤロウ。俺はただなんとなくボケーッとしている風を装った──いや、ていうか、実際ボケーッとしてるわけなんだけどさ。
lines.english: I'm playing Passerby A. Like hell I could say that. I just pretended to be spacing out—or, hell, I actually was spacing out.

lines.japanese: 「なんか考え事？　相談のろうか？」
lines.english: “Thinking about something? Wanna talk?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、んー」
lines.english: “Uh, mm.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと、なに。何なん、この生き物。ひとの話、まるで聞く気なさ気なんですけど」
lines.english: Hey, what the hell? What even is this thing? It's not listening to a word I'm saying.

lines.japanese: 「あー、んー」
lines.english: “Uh, mm.”

lines.japanese: 「よし、今のうちにチューでもしてしまえ」
lines.english: “Fine. I’ll kiss him while I have the chance.”

lines.japanese: 「いやおまえ、ひとがトリップしてる隙にレイプ願望おこすのやめてくんない」
lines.english: “Hey, could you not get the urge to rape me the second I zone out?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃー、ひとン事おいて勝手にトリップすんなしー。てか、なんで急にトリップしてん？」
lines.english: “Then don't wander off into a trance and leave me behind. Why'd you suddenly zone out, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「急にっつうか、だって俺の趣味、柳木原のマンウォッチングとビル林浴だもん」
lines.english: “It wasn't sudden. My hobbies are people-watching in Yanagihara and concrete-jungle bathing.”

lines.japanese: 「び、びるりん……？　なにそれ」
lines.english: “Con-concrete...? What's that?”

lines.japanese: 「森林浴のコンクリートジャングル版」
lines.english: “The urban version of forest bathing.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……財布に優しい趣味だね」
lines.english: “Huh... Easy on the wallet, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「意外とおもしれーんだよ。やってみ」
lines.english: “It's more interesting than you'd think. Try it.”

lines.japanese: 「どーやんの？」
lines.english: “How?”

lines.japanese: お？　意外と興味アリ？
lines.english: Huh? She's actually interested?

lines.japanese: 「目ぇ閉じてボケッとすんだよ」
lines.english: “Close your eyes and go blank.”

lines.japanese: 「こーう？」
lines.english: “Like thiiis?”

lines.japanese: 「そう。で、全体を意識すんの。こう、なんか、でっけえドンブリの底に自分ひとりいるカンジで、そしたら……」
lines.english: “Right. Then take in the whole thing. Imagine you're all alone at the bottom of a gigantic bowl, and then...”

lines.japanese: 「ぷはっ！　なにそれ、新興宗教？」
lines.english: “Pfft! What is this, some new religion?”

lines.japanese: 「ばか、笑うとこじゃねえよ。言ってる方が恥ずかしくなんだろ、てめブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Idiot, it isn’t funny. You’re making me embarrassed I even tried to explain it. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「ごーめん、そんでそんでー？」
lines.english: “Sorry! So then? Then what?”

lines.japanese: やる気なくした。やっぱ通じないもんなのかな、この感覚……。
lines.english: I lost the will to explain. Maybe this feeling just wasn't getting through to her...

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、たとえば始発待ちのホームでさ、ボケーッつって街の方見てると、なんか無性にあのー……なんだ、なんつーか、あの胸にじーんと来るカンジ？　って分かる？」
lines.english: “Listen. Say you’re waiting on the platform for the first train, staring blankly out at the city, and all of a sudden you get this... I don’t know. Your chest sort of swells? You know what I mean?”

lines.japanese: 「あんま最終逃すほど不良じゃないしなー私。あ、でもうん、なんとなく分かる気はするするー」
lines.english: “I'm not enough of a delinquent to miss the last train very often. But, yeah, I feel like I kind of get it.”

lines.japanese: 嘘だ。
lines.english: She was lying.

lines.japanese: 話を合わせようという気遣いは伝わってくるけど、もっと俺の欲しいものが伝わってこない。
lines.english: I could feel the consideration in her attempt to play along. I couldn't feel the thing I wanted from her.

lines.japanese: 俺と香田は合わないんだ。バカ話をしてる分にはそれなりに楽しいけど、そこより先はない。ドン詰まりだ。だから何だって話。
lines.english: Koda and I didn't fit. Trading nonsense with her was fun enough, but there was nothing beyond it. A dead end. So what?

lines.japanese: 「やぁ～ん、私たち気が合う～、隼人きゅ～ん」
lines.english: “Aww, we’re so perfectly in sync, Hayato, sweetie!”

lines.japanese: 「寄りかかんな。重い」
lines.english: “Don't lean on me. You're heavy.”

lines.japanese: 「おっ、重くなーい！　ちゃんと順調に減ってってんの！　もー、女の子にそんな暴言とかマジ信じらんない──」
lines.english: I-I'm not heavy! It's coming down just fine! God, I can't believe you'd say something that awful to a girl—

lines.japanese: 「──お？　なんだこれ？」
lines.english: “—Oh? What's this?”

lines.japanese: 香田が俺のポケットを叩いてる。
lines.english: Koda was patting my pocket.

lines.japanese: 「あん？　なにが……ああ、ゴミだろ」
lines.english: “Hm? What... Oh, probably trash.”

lines.japanese: やつの手を払いのけて、中のものを引っぱりだした。丸めた紙片。名刺みたいな厚さと大きさの──
lines.english: I brushed her hand away and pulled out what was inside. A crumpled scrap of paper, about the thickness and size of a business card—

lines.japanese: 「──ああ、思いだした。ソレきのう、Ｒなんたらの集会で佐久間にもらったやつだ」
lines.english: “—Oh, right. Sakuma gave me that yesterday at the R-whatever meeting.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: ドン引かれた。
lines.english: She was seriously creeped out.

lines.japanese: 「……マジで？　何ソレ、隼人君もしかして、佐久間君たちと仲良くなっちゃったん？」
lines.english: “...Seriously? What's that supposed to mean? Did you make friends with Sakuma and his crowd?”

lines.japanese: やべ、誤解を招く言い方だったか。
lines.english: Crap. Did I phrase that the wrong way?

lines.japanese: 「偶然だ、偶然。誰が好き好んであんな連中に近付くかよ」
lines.english: It was a coincidence, a coincidence. Who'd go near those people on purpose?

lines.japanese: 「俺はＲなんたらともフレイムなんたらとも仲良くしたくねーんで、まあなんか両方から逃げまわってるうちに、まあなんかいろいろあって、まあなんか気付いたら佐久間にソレ渡されてたんだよ」
lines.english: “I don't wanna be friends with the R-whatevers or the Flame-whatevers. I was running away from both, and, well, stuff happened, and then somehow I found Sakuma handing me that.”

lines.japanese: まあなんか適当に説明すると、一度は遠ざかった香田の体がまた戻ってきた。いや近い、戻りすぎだ馬鹿。
lines.english: I gave her some half-assed explanation, and Koda, who'd backed off, came right back. No, too close. You came back too far, idiot.

lines.japanese: 「なーんだ、そーなんだあ。でー、何なんコレ」
lines.english: “Oh, that's all. So what is this?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ。見たけどよく分かんなかった。ま、ゴミだな」
lines.english: “No idea. I looked at it, but it didn't make much sense. Trash, basically.”

lines.japanese: 「どれ、見してみー？　『鷹は舞い降りた』……なんだろ、アドレス付いてるけど……佐久間君のブログかなんかかな」
lines.english: “Here, lemme see. *The Hawk Has Landed*... What's that? There's an address. Maybe Sakuma's blog or something?”

lines.japanese: 「隼人君、このサイト行ってみた？」
lines.english: “Hayato, did you try visiting this site?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああ、いや、よく分かんねーけど……俺インターネットの機械持ってないから」
lines.english: “Huh? No. I don't really get it... I don't own an internet machine.”

lines.japanese: 「あー……ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh... Right.”

lines.japanese: 俺はいま変なことを言ったんだろうか。年寄りに向けるような慈悲深いほほ笑みを返された気がする。
lines.english: Had I said something strange? She gave me what felt like the benevolent smile one reserved for the elderly.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ試しにちょっと見てみっか」
lines.english: “Then let's try looking at it.”

lines.japanese: 香田が無駄にデコられた携帯電話を取りだす。爪が無駄にラメついてる指で、無駄にチャカついてるボタンをかちかち叩きまくった。
lines.english: Koda produced a needlessly decorated cell phone. With fingers covered in needless glitter, she clicked away at needlessly flashy buttons.

lines.japanese: 「ああそうか、最近のケータイはインターネットの機械も入ってんだっけ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Phones these days have internet machines inside them.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、うん……最近でもないんだけど、まあね……」
lines.english: “Uh, yeah... That isn't exactly recent, but sure...”

lines.japanese: またあのあったかい笑顔を向けられた気がする。
lines.english: I felt that same warm smile directed at me again.

lines.japanese: 「なあ。ところでインターネットってどんな形してんの」
lines.english: “Hey. What shape is the internet, anyway?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああほら、繋がったし『鷹は舞い降りた』」
lines.english: “Oh! Look, it connected. *The Hawk Has Landed*.”

lines.japanese: 小さい液晶画面を向けられた。
lines.english: She turned the tiny LCD screen toward me.

lines.japanese: 黒地に赤文字、という目に優しくない絵ヅラが映っていた。
lines.english: Red letters on a black background: a picture calculated to abuse the eyes.

lines.japanese: 「なにコレ」
lines.english: “What is this?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだろ、シュミ悪いデザインだよね。コレはあれかな……ああやっぱり。コレ要は、佐久間君たちのグループ、あのＲなんとかいう、あそこのひとらのホームページみたい──」
lines.english: “I don't know. The design is awful. Maybe this is... Oh, yeah. Basically, it looks like the website for Sakuma's group. Those R-somethings—”

lines.japanese: 「──あっ、違う。ここはメインサイトじゃなくて、特別会員用の裏ページなんだ。えっ、じゃどうしよう、うちら無関係だし、入れたけど本当は入っちゃまずいのかな」
lines.english: “—Oh, wait. This isn't the main site. It's a hidden page for special members. What do we do? We have nothing to do with them. We got in, but maybe we really shouldn't be here.”

lines.japanese: 「さあー」
lines.english: “Who knows.”

lines.japanese: よく分からないし、たぶん分かったとしても俺が興味を持つことはなさそうだ。どうでもいい。そもそも文字が小さくて読む気にならない。
lines.english: I didn't understand it, and even if I had, I doubted I would care. Whatever. The letters were too small to make me want to read them anyway.

lines.japanese: 香田はひとりでしばらくケータイと睨めっこしていた。そんな読みふけるようなことでも書いてあるのか。どうせ佐久間安男のおもしろ下品歌とかじゃないのか。
lines.english: Koda stared at the phone by herself for a while. Was anything there really worth reading that closely? It was probably just Yasuo Sakuma’s funny dirty songs.

lines.japanese: 香田に放置された俺は、いつものビル林浴でもして暇を潰そうと思った。
lines.english: Abandoned by Koda, I decided to pass the time with my usual concrete-jungle bathing.

lines.japanese: しかしＲなんたらの話が出たせいか、ゆうべの事件がチラチラよぎって上手くトリップができない。
lines.english: Maybe because the R-whatevers had come up, last night's events kept flickering across my mind, and I couldn't sink into the trance properly.

lines.japanese: あのあと連中はどうしただろう。とくに負傷の大きな鳳翔や大司教は。
lines.english: What had they done afterward? Especially Kakeru Otori and the Archbishop, who had been badly hurt.

lines.japanese: 「香田、悪い。ついでにちょっと、調べてもらいたいことがあんだけど」
lines.english: “Koda, sorry. While you're at it, there's something I want you to look up.”

lines.japanese: 「え……いまのページで？　ああ、ごめん、もう閉じちゃった……なんか思ったよりキショくて、笑って流せない書き込みとかもあったから……」
lines.english: “What... on that page? Oh, sorry. I already closed it. Some posts were creepier than I expected—things I couldn't just laugh off...”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah?”

lines.japanese: どうやら本気で嫌悪したみたいだ。おもしろ下品歌はやりすぎ下品歌だったのかもしれない。
lines.english: She seemed genuinely disgusted. Maybe the funny-dirty songs had turned into way-too-dirty songs.

lines.japanese: 「俺がもっかい繋いでって言ったら？」
lines.english: “What if I asked you to connect again?”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、嫌かも。あそこに私のケータイのＩＰ履歴、何度も残したくない。なんか気分悪い」
lines.english: “Sorry. I don't think I want to. I don't want my phone's IP showing up in their logs over and over. It makes me feel gross.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう。じゃあいいや」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah? Then forget it.”

lines.japanese: べつにどうしても調べたいわけじゃない。ただちょっとオウムやニワトリの事後が気になっただけだ。
lines.english: It wasn’t as if I absolutely had to investigate. I was only a little curious about what had happened to Parrot Head and Chicken afterward.

lines.japanese: まあ、いい。よっぽどマズイ事態になればそのうち嫌でも耳には入ってくるだろうし、入ってこなければ大したことはなかったって話になる。便りがないのはいい報せだ。
lines.english: Fine. If things had gone truly bad, word would reach me sooner or later whether I liked it or not. If no word came, then nothing serious had happened. No news was good news.

lines.japanese: 「え、どーしても見たい？」
lines.english: “Do you really wanna see it?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そんなでも」
lines.english: “Not that badly.”

lines.japanese: 「どーしても見たかったら漫喫行っときー」
lines.english: “If you absolutely have to, go to a comic-book café.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、そんなでもねーんだって。いいよ、忘れろよ」
lines.english: “I said I don't care that much. Forget it.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、そっか。隼人君、パソコン使ったことない系？」
lines.english: “Oh, I get it. Are you the type who's never used a computer?”

lines.japanese: 「つーか触ったことすらない系」
lines.english: “More the type who's never even touched one.”

lines.japanese: 「ほぉー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 香田はストラップの束を握り、ケータイ本体の方をしばらくぐるぐる回していた。顎をそびやかして、なにやら微妙に上から目線。
lines.english: Koda grabbed the wad of phone charms and spun the phone around and around. Chin up, looking just a little smug.

lines.japanese: 「そしたらネカフェつれてってあげよっかー？　ネットの見方ぐらい教えてあげんしー」
lines.english: “Then want me to take you to an internet café? I can at least teach you how to use the web.”

lines.japanese: なんだネカフェって。ああ、漫画喫茶か。
lines.english: What was a net café? Oh, she meant a comic-book café.

lines.japanese: 「いや、だからインターネットはもういいんだって」
lines.english: “No. I told you, I'm done with the internet.”

lines.japanese: ニワトリやオウムがどーなってようと、俺の知ったこっちゃない。
lines.english: I couldn’t care less what happened to Chicken or Parrot Head.

lines.japanese: 隣りの携帯電話をひょいと覗くぐらいの労力なら使ってもいいが、わざわざ漫喫まで歩いて部屋代払うほどのこっちゃない。
lines.english: I’d spend the effort it took to glance at somebody else’s phone. It wasn’t worth walking all the way to a comic-book café and paying for a booth.

lines.japanese: しかし──
lines.english: However—

lines.japanese: 「はい決定、ネットカフェいくよー！」
lines.english: “Decision made. We're going to an internet café!”

lines.japanese: ──成田工務店の雇用主は勝手に歩きだした。
lines.english: —the girl who’d hired Narita Construction had already started off without asking me.

lines.japanese: 「ちょーちょーおっちゃん、その雑誌拾ったの。１００円で売ってくんない」
lines.english: “Hey, old-timer, did you find that magazine? Wanna sell it to me for a hundred yen?”

lines.japanese: 「隼人はやくこい」
lines.english: “Hayato, hurry up.”

lines.japanese: 聞こえないふりも通用せず引きずられていった。すでにこいつ、自分が行きたいだけだろ。
lines.english: Pretending I didn't hear her got me nowhere, and she dragged me along. At this point, she just wanted to go herself.

lines.japanese: 形としてはやつの付き合いだが、費用は自分持ちだとのこと。
lines.english: Officially I was accompanying her, but apparently I had to pay my own admission.

lines.japanese: 日給２４０円。部屋代１時間４００円～。出費のがデカいじゃねーか。
lines.english: Daily wage: 240 yen. Booth fee: 400 yen an hour and up. I was losing money on the job.

lines.japanese: 「いなくなるんだったら、楽しい想い出できるだけ作っとこうよ」
lines.english: “If you're going away, let's make as many happy memories as we can first.”

lines.japanese: やつが何気なく漏らしたその一言は、どこまで本気だったんだろう。
lines.english: How serious was she about that thing she'd just casually let slip?
